concerns.title: Trapped gas at the stuffing box — BRYAN MEDLIN and MICHAEL JOBE, XTO, WINDHAM 7 #6, 8:17 AM to 11:16 AM, jobs 37083 and 37084. Medlin's narrative reads
concerns.text: : "On the second break of containment there were some trapped gases in the stuffing box, the well was still on a vacuum at this point." Jobe, the second technician on the same well, recorded only "There was pressure on the stuffing box" and left his "Details if Any" close-out blank. No numeric gas reading appears on either form, and neither technician recorded a stop-work or a corrective action. Follow-up: confirm with both technicians what was detected, what the readings were, and whether the crew was placed on air — this is the one entry today that describes gas actually present rather than absent. doc.text: Bottle Hydro Dates and cascade pressures

BREY RASCO, H2S daily, Mitsui, Lipsey 1H, 1:25 PM. Both "Pressure on Cascade System" and "Bottle Hydro Dates" are blank. The board gives AT# 140 for that row, so a trailer is named and these fields are in scope. Re-read from the source PDF: the form carries sensor battery levels "11.8. 10.8. 9.5. 11.2. 11.3. 11.3. 10.7. 10.8" and then both cascade labels with no value against either. The same form also shows no capture at all against ELSA Photos or against any of the six air-trailer photo slots.

MICHAEL JOBE, Trailer Readiness Form, trailer 606, 1:58 PM. Entries #1 through #4 each read exactly "7-25" — a hydro date with no pressure. Entries #5 through #10 read "Na" and are not findings. This is a valid finding: the combined field needs both values.

RUBEN ROJO, Trailer Readiness Form, trailer 601, 11:21 AM. Entries #1 through #4 are complete — "5/24 4500", "2/23 4500", "1/25 4500", "1/25 4500". Entries #5 through #10 read "N", "N", "N", "M", "N", "M". A single letter is not the same as "N/A", so these six positions are reported as unreadable rather than assumed empty. Note the #2 hydro date of 2/23 is the oldest recorded on any trailer today.
DAWSON DRAKE, Trailer Readiness Form, trailer 607, 2:59 PM. Entries #1 through #4 are complete. Entry #5 reads "Na"; entries #6 through #10 read "N" and are likewise reported as unreadable.

ANDREW BAILEY, Trailer Readiness Form, trailer 501, 3:32 PM. Entry #1 reads "All 3/23 and 2500psi" with #2 through #10 all "Na". The entry does carry both a pressure and a hydro date so it is not a missing-value finding, but the ten bottle positions were not recorded individually as the form asks.

BRIANDA SANDOVAL, Trailer Readiness Form, trailer 504, 4:58 PM. All six charged positions carry both values — "2100 +* 04/23", "2200 +* 04/23", "2200 +* 04/23", "2100 +* 04/23", "2000 +* 04/23" and "900 +* 04/23". clean.text: Technicians whose submissions carry nothing requiring attention: JUSTIN PACK, whose H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form for Southwest Operating at Hughes #1 is the most complete of the six filed, with both cascade fields populated and every photograph captured on the day; 1099 JUSTIN FONTENOT, who filed a Trailer Inspection Form for trailer 601 and air job 37309 at Davidson-Hale, both complete and both fully photographed on the day; JACOB HERNANDEZ for air job 37319 at University Blk 9; ALEXANDER CLUBB for two Trailer Inspection Forms on trailer 125 and air job 37157 at Buchanan H #1; KEELAN HAMMER and Kelby Hammer for the Patriot Processing and Charles Lawson training job forms; and JERRY GONZALES for his Trailer Inspection Form on trailer 503, which is complete and current even though his two Roman 22B job submissions are listed as missing above.

Trailer forms of both kinds and the equipment sections of the H2S daily are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside the images and not as text, so none of them has been checked here. One further limitation today: the H2S daily from 1099 Marcos Morales could not be opened at all because its PDF exceeds the mail connector's size limit, so nothing on that form — his FR answer, his cascade entries, his photo dates — has been verified. It will need opening directly in Outlook.

91 of 91 submissions read, 90 of 91 attachments successfully opened. The job board was available: the 11/24/2026 boards emailed by Blake Walton at 10:11 AM were used, and 53 manned board rows were checked for coverage — 40 on the Permian Basin board and 13 on the ArkLaTex board. This run began at 11:06 PM Central, before the Central day closed, so any form submitted in the final hour of 11/24 is not in these counts. Missing Trailer Readiness Forms and missing night-shift H2S dailies are the findings most often resolved by a late submission, and the Dennis Easley night-shift gap and the trailer 503 readiness form are the two most likely to land after this report was written.
